text: 用搜索引擎查找需要的信息，不要关注热榜和推荐内容就行。
en: Use search engines to find the information you need; just don't follow hot lists and recommended content.

text: 真正的茧房不是算法建的，是你自己盖的。
en: The real cocoon is not built by algorithms; you build it yourself.

text: 平台只是顺着你走。
en: Platforms just follow your lead.

text: 刷到不同意见，手指比脑子快，一划就过去了；刷到顺耳的，多看两眼还顺手点个赞。
en: When you scroll to a dissenting opinion, your fingers are faster than your brain — one swipe and it's gone; when you scroll to something pleasing to the ear, you look a couple more times and casually give it a like.

text: 久而久之，喂到你面前的当然全是一个调子。
en: Over time, what is fed to you is naturally all one tune.

text: 想出去，别急着卸载app，先改掉这个条件反射。
en: If you want to get out, don't rush to uninstall apps — first change this conditioned reflex.

text: 刻意挑几个让你别扭的说法看完整，找出它最有道理的那句，再问自己一句：万一是我错了呢？
en: Deliberately pick a few statements that make you uncomfortable and read them through, find the most reasonable sentence in them, and then ask yourself: what if I'm wrong?

text: 茧房不怕你信息少，怕的是你压根没打算出来。
en: The cocoon is not afraid that you have little information; it fears that you have no intention of coming out at all.

text: 为什么你讨厌信息茧房？
en: Why do you hate information cocoons?

text: 信息茧房很多时候是帮你过滤掉了毒素。
en: Information cocoons often help you filter out toxins.

text: 我经常看国内的人民日报、新华社，也看cnn这种左翼主流媒体，还看fox这种明显偏向川普的。
en: I often read domestic People's Daily and Xinhua, as well as left-leaning mainstream media like CNN, and Fox, which is clearly biased towards Trump.

text: 我很清楚做得最好的是人民日报和新华社，他们避免了老百姓接触到很多不良信息。
en: I am well aware that the best performers are People's Daily and Xinhua — they prevent ordinary people from coming into contact with a lot of bad information.

text: 我们国家对一些书籍的删改也很不错，难道你想让《the dictator’s handbook》、奥威尔和福山的那些书，未经删改直接原文出版，来毒害我们善良的老百姓？
en: Our country's deletion and editing of some books is also quite good. Do you want books like The Dictator's Handbook, Orwell's and Fukuyama's books, to be published directly in their original text without deletions, to poison our kind ordinary people?

text: 多刷知乎，我发现任何主流声音，知乎都有反对的，知乎帮助你辩证看待
en: Scrolling Zhihu more, I find that for any mainstream voice, Zhihu has opposition — Zhihu helps you view things dialectically.

text: 信息茧房问题，实际上是一个人的三观问题
en: The information cocoon problem is actually a person's values problem.

text: 你意识到信息茧房存在的时候，基本上就走出了信息茧房。
en: When you realise the information cocoon exists, you have basically walked out of the information cocoon.

text: 哪怕你不打算跳槽，手机里也永远留一个BOSS直聘。
en: Even if you don't plan to switch jobs, always keep a Boss Zhipin app on your phone.

text: 没事刷下所在的行业、上下游行业，以及那些所谓风口行业的真实JD和底薪。
en: When you have nothing to do, scroll through the real JDs and base salaries of your industry, upstream and downstream industries, and those so-called booming industries.

text: 七点新闻里天天喊产业升级和红利，那tm是吹给韭菜看的；挂出来的薪水，才是真实定价。
en: The industrial upgrading and dividends shouted about in the 7 o'clock news — that's damn hype for the leeks to watch; the salaries posted are the real pricing.

text: 睡前别老刷微博热搜，就看“文书网”随便盲抽5份判决书。
en: Before bed, don't keep scrolling Weibo hot searches — just look at 'Wenshu Net' and randomly draw 5 judgment documents.

text: 你就主要看民间借贷纠纷、离婚财产分割、基层劳务索赔。
en: You mainly look at private lending disputes, divorce property division, and grassroots labour claims.

text: 热搜是公关和情绪，而判决书那就是人性、算计和底层互害。
en: Hot searches are PR and emotions, while judgment documents are human nature, calculation, and bottom-level mutual harm.

text: 看上三个月，绝对对真实社会的认知上升一个层次。
en: After reading for three months, your understanding of real society will definitely rise a level.

text: 买包华子，去跟你小区楼下开了五六年的小卖部、沙县小吃或者五金店老板聊半个小时，这事我以前跑步时候最爱干。
en: Buy a pack of Zhonghua, and go chat for half an hour with the owner of the small shop, Shaxian snacks stall, or hardware store downstairs in your neighbourhood that's been open for five or six years — this is what I loved doing most when I used to run.

text: 问问房租涨跌、水电费、进货价波动啥的，，听小老板骂两句娘，比看十份投行研报都管用。
en: Ask about rent rises and falls, water and electricity bills, purchase price fluctuations, and listen to the small boss curse a couple of times — more useful than reading ten investment bank research reports.

text: 戒掉所有自媒体的政策解读，直接去翻你们市/区政府网站的“年度财政预算执行报告”和“公共资源交易招标网”。
en: Quit all self-media policy interpretations, and directly flip through your city/district government website's 'Annual Fiscal Budget Execution Report' and 'Public Resources Trading and Bidding Website'.

text: 你就顺着表格往下看，看看今年的真金白银到底砸给了哪个新区的基建、转移给了哪家城投公司、砍掉了哪块的民生支出。
en: Just follow the tables down, and see where this year's real money was actually spent — which new district's infrastructure, which city investment company it was transferred to, which livelihood expenditure was cut.

text: 钱的流向是最诚实的，看懂了政府的账本，起码了解你们城市运转一般逻辑。
en: The flow of money is the most honest. Once you understand your city's account books, you at least understand the general logic of how your city operates.

text: 挑三个你极度讨厌、价值观完全相左，但确实在社会上赚到了大钱的人。
en: Pick three people you extremely dislike, whose values are completely opposite to yours, but who have indeed made big money in society.

text: 强迫自己捏着鼻子，去把他们的发家史和访谈看完。
en: Force yourself to hold your nose and read through their rise-to-riches stories and interviews.

text: 放下你的道德洁癖，去拆解这帮傻逼到底切中了哪些人的痛点，完成了怎样的商业闭环。
en: Put aside your moral cleanliness, and dissect how these dumbasses hit the pain points of which people, and completed what kind of commercial closed loop.

text: 理解并解剖你不认同的运行规则，
en: Understand and dissect operating rules you do not agree with,

text: 有人喜欢的话，我再写点。
en: If people like it, I'll write more.

text: 有的是我自己个人习惯，有的是我听几个大佬在闲聊时候听到的，分享给爱看干货朋友。
en: Some are my own personal habits, some I heard from a few big shots chatting idly — sharing with friends who love practical content.

text: 不要被自媒体被动的推荐，自己主动的选择！
en: Don't be passively recommended by self-media; actively choose yourself!

text: 推荐几个网站：
en: Recommend a few websites:

text: 1. 中国新闻网
en: 1. China News Service

text: 别以为只有公务员看！
en: Don't think only civil servants read it!

text: 这里是最权威的政策风向标。
en: This is the most authoritative policy weathervane.

text: 2. [城市名]+发布
en: 2. [City name] + Fabu

text: 直通本地官方情报站！
en: Direct access to the local official intelligence station!

text: 拆迁、学区、落户新政第一时间知晓。
en: Demolition, school districts, and new settlement policies known at the first opportunity.

text: 3. [城市名]+本地宝
en: 3. [City name] + Bendibao

text: 领补贴、查社保、找攻略，一键Get全城实用信息，省钱又省心。
en: Get subsidies, check social security, find guides — one click gets all the city's practical information, saving money and worry.

text: 4. 今日热榜
en: 4. Today's Hot List

text: 全网热搜聚合器！
en: Aggregator of hot searches across the internet!

text: 微博、抖音、知乎等全网各大媒体的热点一目了然。
en: Hot topics from Weibo, Douyin, Zhihu and other major media across the internet at a glance.

text: 5. 雪球
en: 5. Xueqiu

text: 投资人的实战场！
en: The actual battlefield for investors!

text: 看大牛逻辑、读财报解读。
en: Read big shots' logic, read financial report interpretations.

text: 最后，终极搞钱三件套：36氪+虎嗅+钛媒体
en: Finally, the ultimate money-making trio: 36Kr + Huxiu + TMTpost.

text: 早看36氪：盯融资快讯，抓下一个风口；
en: Read 36Kr in the morning: watch financing news, catch the next trend;

text: 午刷虎嗅：扒商业潜规则，看透巨头博弈；
en: Scroll Huxiu at noon: expose unspoken business rules, see through giant rivalries;

text: 晚啃钛媒体：死磕技术趋势，预判未来赛道。
en: Study TMTpost in the evening: focus on technology trends, predict future tracks.

text: 从逻辑上说，这个世界上只有美国配谈信息茧房，中国根本不可能实现国家范围的信息茧房，很多人连这个基础问题都理解不了。
en: Logically speaking, in this world only America is qualified to talk about information cocoons; China simply cannot achieve a nationwide information cocoon. Many people cannot even understand this basic issue.

text: 总有人说“简中互联网信息茧房balabala”，动动脑子，以中国的宣传能力，即便想塑造信息茧房都没那个能力，因为中国人根本不可能看不见来自美国的宣传内容，简中互联网至少有中美两个信息源，你见过漏了两个大洞的茧？
en: There are always people saying 'simplified Chinese internet information cocoon blah blah blah' — use your brain: with China's propaganda capability, even if it wanted to shape an information cocoon, it doesn't have that ability, because Chinese people simply cannot fail to see propaganda content from America. The simplified Chinese internet has at least two information sources, Chinese and American — have you ever seen a cocoon with two big holes in it?

text: 不仅中国，俄罗斯乃至西欧国家、日本都不配建立信息茧房，因为他们连中国都不如，中国好歹有道墙能打压美国声音的音量，这几个难兄难弟直接被美国社交媒体喇叭堵门，还有没有本土舆论还要打个问号，别说建立信息茧房，不跟美国人住在同一个茧房里就谢天谢地了。
en: Not only China — Russia, Western European countries, and Japan are not even qualified to build information cocoons, because they are worse off than China. China at least has a wall that can dampen the volume of American voices; these fellow sufferers have American social media loudspeakers directly blocking their doors — whether they even have local public opinion is questionable, let alone building information cocoons. Not living in the same cocoon as Americans would be something to thank heavens for.

text: 拥有垄断信息源能力的人在制造信息茧房，而不是反过来由用户自己给自己制造茧房，互联网时代网民并没有筛选信息的能力和资格，我们看到的是别人想让我们看的。
en: Those with the ability to monopolise information sources are the ones creating information cocoons, not the other way around with users creating cocoons for themselves. In the internet era, netizens do not have the ability or qualification to filter information; what we see is what others want us to see.

text: 这个世界上有且仅有一个地方能够实现完全遮蔽来自外界的声音，那就是美国，更准确的说是美国西海岸，他们的能力强大到连本国铁锈带的声音都被屏蔽了，部分美国民主党支持者完全活在别人修筑的茧房里。
en: There is one and only one place in this world that can achieve complete shielding from outside voices, and that is America — more precisely, America's West Coast. Their capability is so strong that even the voices of their own Rust Belt are blocked. Some American Democratic Party supporters live entirely in cocoons built by others.

text: 而在中国这个整天吵成一团的网络环境里，谁能真的掉进茧房？
en: And in China's online environment, which is noisy all day long, who can really fall into a cocoon?

text: 互相冲突的信息到处都是，会造成偏执的是你自己内心傲慢，选择性无视了其他信息，这种人不是茧房里的虫子，而是把脑袋埋起来的鸵鸟，井底之蛙尚且有看到天空的机会，鸵鸟没有。
en: Conflicting information is everywhere. What causes paranoia is your own inner arrogance, selectively ignoring other information. Such people are not insects in a cocoon, but ostriches burying their heads. Even a frog at the bottom of a well has a chance to see the sky; ostriches do not.

text: 想要避免也容易，如果看见某个新闻、某个回答惹你不高兴，只要还有实际内容，至少先看完再说，兼听则明。
en: Avoiding it is also easy: if you see a piece of news or an answer that makes you unhappy, as long as it still has actual content, at least finish reading it first — listening to both sides makes one enlightened.
